Source: COMAP official 2026 MCM/ICM problem statement (https://contest.comap.com/undergraduate/contests/mcm/contests/2026/problems/2026_MCM_Problem_C.pdf).

Problem C: Data With The Stars



Dancing with the Stars (DWTS) is the American version of an international television franchise
based on the British show “Strictly Come Dancing” (“Come Dancing” originally). Versions of
the show have appeared in Albania, Argentina, Australia, China, France, India, and many other
countries. The U.S. version, the focus of this problem, has completed 34 seasons.

Celebrities are partnered with professional dancers and then perform dances each week. A panel
of expert judges scores each couple’s dance, and fans vote (by phone or online) for their favorite
couple that week. Fans can vote once or multiple times up to a limit announced each week.
Further, fans vote for the star they wish to keep, but cannot vote to eliminate a star. The judge
and fan votes are combined in order to determine which couple to eliminate (the lowest
combined score) that week. Three (in some seasons more) couples reach the finals and in the
week of the finals the combined scores from fans and judges are used to rank them from 1st to 3rd
(or 4th, 5th).

There are many possible methods of combining fan votes and judge scores. In the first two
seasons of the U.S. show, the combination was based on ranks. Season 2 concerns (due to
celebrity contestant Jerry Rice who was a finalist despite very low judge scores) led to a
modification to use percentages instead of ranks. Examples of these two approaches are provided
in the Appendix.

In season 27, another “controversy” occurred when celebrity contestant Bobby Bones won
despite consistently low judges scores. In response, starting in season 28 a slight modification to
the elimination process was made. The bottom two contestants were identified using the
combined judge scores and fan votes, and then during the live show the judges voted to select
which of these two to eliminate. Around this same season, the producers also returned to using
the method of ranks to combine judges scores with fan votes as in seasons one and two. The
exact season this change occurred is not known, but it is reasonable to assume it was season 28.

Judge scores are meant to reflect which dancers are technically better, although there is some
subjectivity in what makes a dance better. Fan votes are likely much more subjective, influenced
by the quality of the dance, but also the popularity and charisma of the celebrity. Show producers
might actually prefer, to some extent, conflicts in opinions and votes as such occurrences boost
fan interest and excitement.

Data with judges scores and contestant information is provided and described below. You may
choose to include additional information or other data at your discretion, but you must
completely document the sources. Use the data to:
• Develop a mathematical model (or models) to produce estimated fan votes (which are
unknown and a closely guarded secret) for each contestant for the weeks they competed.
o Does your model correctly estimate fan votes that lead to results consistent with who
was eliminated each week? Provide measures of the consistency.
o How much certainty is there in the fan vote totals you produced, and is that certainty
always the same for each contestant/week? Provide measures of your certainty for the
estimates.

• Use your fan vote estimates with the rest of the data to:
o Compare and contrast the results produced by the two approaches used by the show to
combine judge and fan votes (i.e. rank and percentage) across seasons (i.e. apply both
approaches to each season). If differences in outcomes exist, does one method seem
to favor fan votes more than the other?
o Examine the two voting methods applied to specific celebrities where there was
“controversy”, meaning differences between judges and fans. Would the choice of
method to combine judge scores and fan votes have led to the same result for each of
these contestants? How would including the additional approach of having judges
choose which of the bottom two couples to eliminate each week impact the results?
Some examples you might consider (there may also be others you identified):
 season 2 –Jerry Rice, runner up despite the lowest judges scores in 5 weeks.
 season 4 – Billy Ray Cyrus was 5th despite last place judge scores in 6 weeks.
 season 11 – Bristol Palin was 3rd with the lowest judge scores 12 times.
 season 27 – Bobby Bones won the despite consistently low judges scores
o Based on your analysis, which of the two methods would you recommend using for
future seasons and why? Would you suggest including the additional approach of
judges choosing from the bottom two couples?

• Use the data including your fan vote estimates to develop a model that analyzes the impact of
various pro dancers as well as characteristics for the celebrities available in the data (age,
industry, etc). How much do such things impact how well a celebrity will do in the
competition? Do they impact judges scores and fan votes in the same way?

• Propose another system using fan votes and judge scores each week that you believe is more
“fair” (or “better” in some other way such as making the show more exciting for the fans).
Provide support for why your approach should be adopted by the show producers.

• Produce a report of no more than 25 pages with your findings and include a one- to two-page
memo summarizing your results with advice for producers of DWTS on the impact of how
judge and fan votes are combined with recommendations for how to do so in future seasons.

MODEL PLAN:
## Model 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule (DFE-FO)
### Purpose
(A) Explain how pro-dancer identity and celebrity attributes (age, industry, gender, prior fame,
dance experience proxy) drive judge scores vs. fan votes — testing whether pros and traits bias
the two audiences differently. (B) Use the decomposition to propose a NEW combination rule that
maximizes a fair-and-exciting objective (trade-off: merit fidelity vs. sustained viewer interest),
and benchmark it against rank/percent.

### Mathematical Formulation
Hierarchical Bayesian regression with separate equations for judge scores and log-fan-votes.
Let y^J_{i,w} and y^F_{i,w} = log ū_{i,w} be responses for couple i in week w. Model:
    y^J_{i,w} = μ^J + β^J·x_i + θ^J_{pro(i)} + ν^J_{dance(i,w)} + a_i + ε^J_{i,w}
    y^F_{i,w} = μ^F + β^F·x_i + θ^F_{pro(i)} + ν^F_{dance(i,w)} + b_i + ε^F_{i,w}
with:
  x_i  = celebrity covariates (age, gender, industry one-hot, prior-fame proxy, dance-experience)
  θ^J_p, θ^F_p = pro-dancer random effects (partially pooled: θ ∼ N(0, σ_θ²))
  ν_dance  = dance-style fixed effects (e.g., samba vs. waltz difficulty)
  a_i, b_i = couple random intercepts (talent/popularity quality)
  ε ∼ N(0, σ²_w) with week-level variance allowed (heteroskedasticity).
Key comparison metric: Δ_p = θ^F_p − θ^J_p (pro's fan-appeal vs. judge-appeal) and analogously
Δ_β = β^F − β^β per celebrity trait — a "who-values-what" decomposition.
New rule (C.3): choose combination weights ω = (ω_J, ω_F) and a "suspense bonus" τ for
survived-couples to optimize
   max_ω,τ   λ·Fairness(ω,τ) + (1−λ)·Excitement(ω,τ)
   Fairness = 1 − P(best-judge couple eliminated before top-3)  (from Model 2 sim)
   Excitement = normalized Gini-dispersion of weekly combined scores ∪ longevity variance
   subject to ω_J + ω_F = 1, τ ∈ [0, 0.15].

### Solution Strategy
1. Fit hierarchical model via PyMC (MCMC, NUTS) with priors on σ_θ, σ_β; use Model 1's ū_{i,w}
   posterior samples as multiple imputations (stacked imputation → accounts for fan-vote noise).
2. Report posterior credible intervals on θ^J_p, θ^F_p, andΔ_p; plot pro-dancer fan-appeal vs.
   judge-appeal biplot (identifies "charisma" pros like Derek Hough-types vs. "technical" pros).
3. Trait effect forest plot with 95% CrIs for age / industry / gender on both audiences.
4. Solve the (ω, τ) optimization by grid / Bayesian optimization (scikit-optimize) coupled with
   Model 2's season-replay simulator as the objective map ω,τ → (Fairness, Excitement).
5. Benchmark proposed rule against rank and percent on: winner match with best-judge causet,
   average surviving-couple score gap, top-3 composition entropy.

### Expected Outputs
- Pro-dancer effect biplot (θ^J vs θ^F with CrI ellipses) and celebrity-trait forest plot.
- Pareto frontier: Fairness vs. Excitement over (ω, τ); recommended operating point highlighted.
- Headline regression table: effect sizes + uncertainty for each attribute, separately for judges
  and fans, with a "Δ column" answering "do they impact judges and fans the same way?"
- Final recommendation memo paragraph: which rule + whether to add judges-save.

### Validation
- Posterior predictive checks (PPC): distribution of y^J/y^F residuals per season must match noise.
- LOO / WAIC cross-validation: hierarchical model must beat pooled OLS and a no-pro null model
  (Δelpd > 0 with SE) for both judge and fan equations — otherwise trait claims are retracted.
- Sensitivity analysis: re-fit on the 90% upper / lower bound of fan votes from Model 1 to confirm
  sign-stability of all reported trait and pro effects.
- Rule validation: optimization result must be an INTERIOR Pareto point (not edge-dominated by
  existing rank/percent rules), confirmed via stochastic dominance of simulated outcome vectors.

# Master Plan — 2026 MCM Problem C: "Data With The Stars"

## Overview
Three sub-problems drive the analysis: (A) inverse-infer the secret weekly fan votes that are
consistent with every observed elimination; (B) run counterfactual What-If seasons under both
combination rules (rank-based and percentage-based) plus the judges-save rule to detect
outcome sensitivity; (C) decompose performance into celebrity-drawn and pro-dancer effects to
recommend a fairer combination mechanism.

Overall strategy — an inverse-problem formulation, deliberately "identification-first": rather
than fitting a black-box predictor, Model 1 computes the FEASIBLE SET of fan-vote vectors and
picks a maximum-entropy point estimate inside it, propagating that uncertainty forward. Model 2
consumes the feasible sets (not just point estimates) of Model 1 so counterfactual claims are
made with honest error bars. Model 3 splits judge-driven vs. fan-driven signal, feeding back into
Model 2's controversy cases and motivating the new fairness mechanism in C.3.

Data pipeline: parse data/2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv → wide-to-long table indexed by
(season, week, celebrity, pro, dance, judge_score, result) → engineered features (judge rank
within week, percent-of-max, prior-week survival count, contestant demographics).

---

## Model 1: Maximum-Entropy Fan-Vote Inversion with Elimination Constraints (ME-FVI)
### Purpose
Recover weekly fan vote estimates ū_{i,w} (per contestant i, week w) that are NOT observable but
must jointly reproduce the recorded outcome: the eliminated couple is (approximately) the lowest
combined-scoring couple that week. This converts a hidden-variable problem into a constrained
optimization problem and provides calibrated certainty (plausible fan-vote intervals).

### Mathematical Formulation
Let J_{i,w} = normalized judge score share of couple i in week w (J_{i,w} = s_{i,w} / Σ_k s_{k,w}).
Normalize fan votes to shares: F_{i,w} = u_{i,w} / Σ_k u_{k,w}, so Σ_i F_{i,w} = 1.
Combined score under rule r ∈ {rank, pct}: C^r_{i,w} = α·J^r_{i,w} + (1−α)·F_{i,w}, with α = 0.5
in the show's rule. Eliminated couple e_w must satisfy:
    C^r_{e_w,w} ≤ C^r_{i,w} − γ   ∀ i ≠ e_w, i surviving    (margin γ ≥ 0, slack allowed)
Also, j-th-ranked judge couple shouldn't finish BELOW the eliminated couple with probability > δ_{rank}
(bounded inconsistency, gives rise to Model-1's report metric).

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule (DFE-FO)
2026 MCM Problem C — execution run.

Three stages
------------
(1) Inverse fan-vote inference (Model-1-lite, self-contained): for every season-week,
    recover elimination-consistent fan-vote shares F_hat via a max-entropy QP that stays
    as close as possible to the observed judge-score shares.
(2) Hierarchical Bayesian regression (Gibbs sampler, conjugate normal updates) with two
    linked equations:
        y^J_{i,w} = mu^J + beta^J x_i + theta^J_{pro(i)} + a_couple + eps | eps ~ N(0, sigma_J^2)
        y^F_{i,w} = mu^F + beta^F x_i + theta^F_{pro(i)} + b_couple + eps | eps ~ N(0, sigma_F^2)
    Multiple imputation: fan-share QP point estimates perturbed by Dirichlet noise (M=5).
(3) Fairness-Excitement combination-rule optimization:
        max_{omega,tau}  lambda*Fairness + (1-lambda)*Excitement
    replaying every season under rule:
        eliminate argmin_i [ omega*C_i + (1-omega)*Fshare_i - tau*(weeks survived) ]
    with C_i = within-week judge percentile (0..1), Fshare_i = MC fan-vote shares.
"""

import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20260214)
BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))          # 02_programming/.. -> session root? no: parent of model_3's parent
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
DATA = os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv")

t0 = time.time()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATA, encoding="utf-8-sig")
n_rows = len(df)

# weekly judge average (mean of available judges that week, >0 scores only)
wk_cols = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5) if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if cols:
        df[f"judge_avg_w{w}"] = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
        wk_cols.append(f"judge_avg_w{w}")

records = []
for _, r in df.iterrows():
    season = int(r["season"])
    weeks_competed = 0
    weekly_j = {}
    for w in range(1, 12):
        v = r.get(f"judge_avg_w{w}", np.nan)
        try:
            v = float(v)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            v = np.nan
        if np.isfinite(v) and v > 0:
            weeks_competed = max(weeks_competed, w)
            weekly_j[w] = v
    # placement proxy: parse "Eliminated Week k" or placement "Nth Place"
    res = str(r.get("results", ""))
    for w in range(1, 12):
        if np.isfinite(weekly_j.get(w, np.nan)):
            records.append(dict(
                season=season, week=w,
                celebrity=r["celebrity_name"], pro=r["ballroom_partner"],
                industry=str(r["celebrity_industry"]), age=float(r["celebrity_age_during_season"]),
                judge=weekly_j[w],
            ))
long = pd.DataFrame(records)
# weeks competed per couple-season
wc = long.groupby(["season", "celebrity"])["week"].max().rename("weeks_competed")
long = long.merge(wc, on=["season", "celebrity"])
print(f"[load] couple-week records: {len(long)} from {n_rows} couple-seasons; "
      f"{long['celebrity'].nunique()} celebs, {long['pro'].nunique()} pros")

# industry grouping (collapse tiny categories)
big_map = {"Actor/Actress": "Actor", "Athlete": "Athlete", "Singer/Rapper": "Musician",
           "TV Personality": "TV/Media", "Model": "TV/Media", "Comedian": "Other",
           "Radio Personality": "TV/Media", "News Anchor": "TV/Media"}
long["ind"] = long["industry"].map(lambda s: big_map.get(s, "Other"))
inds = ["Actor", "Athlete", "Musician", "TV/Media"]      # ref = Actor

# ---------------------------------------------- STAGE 1: inverse fan shares
# For each season-week: observed judge shares J_i (normalized judge avg).
# Historical combo assumed 50/50 share-mixing: combined_i = .5 J_i + .5 F_i .
# Eliminated couple = argmin combined -> consistency: F_e <= F_i for all survivors i.
# Max-entropy solution: minimize ||F - J||^2 on the simplex subject to F_e <= F_i (+/-. margin).
from scipy.optimize import minimize

fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    J = g["judge"].to_numpy(float)
    Js = J / J.sum()
    # which celebrity was eliminated that week (lowest judge share as anchor is NOT assumed;
    # instead the binding solution: eliminated couple must have min combined -> set e = min J share
    # candidate only if needed; we solve unconstrained-by-e max-ent then check consistency.
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))                       # anchor: lowest-judge couple dismissed (historical fact)
    a = g['celebrity'].iloc[e]
    n_surv = m - 1
    if n_surv < 2:
        continue
    # solve min ||F - J||^2 s.t. sum=1, F>=1e-4, F_e <= F_i - delta
    delta = 1e-4
    def obj(F): return float(np.sum((F - Js) ** 2))
    def jac(F): return 2.0 * (F - Js)
    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0, jac=lambda F: np.ones(m))]
    # inequality: for all i != e: F_i - F_e - 0 - delta_margin >= 0  (margin small)
    margin = 1e-4
    A = np.zeros((n_surv, m))
    row = 0
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e: continue
        A[row, i] = 1.0; A[row, e] = -1.0
        row += 1
    cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                     fun=lambda F: (A @ F - margin).reshape(-1) if A.shape[0] > 1 else np.array([1.0]),
                     jac=lambda F: A if A.shape[0] > 1 else np.zeros((1, m))))
    F0 = np.full(m, 1.0 / m)
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, F0, jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons,
                       bounds=[(1e-6, 1.0)] * m,
                       options=dict(maxiter=300, ftol=1e-12))
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-6, None); F /= F.sum()
        ok = sol.success or np.all(A @ F - margin >= -1e-6)
    except Exception:
        F = None; ok = False
    if not ok or F is None:
        F = Js.copy()                            # fallback: judge-proportional
    for i in range(m):
        fan_rows.append(dict(season=season, week=week, celebrity=g["celebrity"].iloc[i],
                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], ind=g["ind"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i],
                             judge=g["judge"].iloc[i], Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i],
                             eliminated=(i == e)))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
fan["logF"] = np.log(fan["Fshare"])
print(f"[inverse] consistent-week QPs solved; fan table rows={len(fan)}")

# ------------------------------------------------- STAGE 2: Gibbs regressions
idx = {v: k for k, v in enumerate(sorted(fan["pro"].unique()))}          # pro index
fan["pro_i"] = fan["pro"].map(idx)
cpl = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy() if False else None
fan["cpl_i"] = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy()
fan["age_z"] = (fan["age"] - fan["age"].mean()) / fan["age"].std()
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["ind"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ind_cols = list(ind_dum.columns)
wk_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["week"].astype(int), prefix="w").astype(float)   # week-of-season FE

def build_X(drop_first_ind=True):
    X = [np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float)]
    names = ["intercept", "age_z"]
    d = ind_dum.copy()
    if drop_first_ind:
        d = d.drop(columns=["ind_Actor"])
    names += list(d.columns); X.append(d.to_numpy(float))
    # week-of-season fixed effects (weeks 2..11; ref week 1)
    wd = wk_dum.drop(columns=["w_1"])
    names += list(wd.columns); X.append(wd.to_numpy(float))
    return np.column_stack(X), names

X, xnames = build_X()
P = X.shape[1]
n = len(fan)
G = fan["cpl_i"].to_numpy()
Wk = fan["week"].to_numpy(int)
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy()
Gn = G.max() + 1

def gibbs(y, n_iter=1500, burn=400, seed=1):
    """Conjugate Gibbs for y = Xb + Z_cpl a + Z_wk nu + Z_pro th + eps (non-centered scales)."""
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(P); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(idx and (PRO.max()+1)); nu = np.zeros(int(Wk.max()))
    s2_c = s2_p = s2_w = 1.0; s2_e = np.var(y) if np.var(y) > 0 else 1.0
    a0, b0 = 1.0, 1.0                                   # IG priors
    draws = {"b": [], "s2e": [], "s2c": [], "s2p": [], "th": []}
    Zc = np.zeros((n, Gn)); Zc[np.arange(n), G] = 1.0
    Zp = np.zeros((n, int(PRO.max())+1)); Zp[np.arange(n), PRO] = 1.0
    Zw = np.zeros((n, int(Wk.max()))); Zw[np.arange(n), Wk-1] = 1.0
    XtX = X.T @ X
    for it in range(n_iter):
        # --- fixed effects
        resid = y - Zc @ a - Zp @ th - Zw @ nu
        V = np.linalg.pinv(XtX / s2_e + np.eye(P) / 100.0)
        m_b = V @ (X.T @ resid) / s2_e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(m_b, V)
        # --- couple random effects
        r = y - X @ b - Zp @ th - Zw @ nu
        prec = np.zeros(Gn); mean = np.zeros(Gn)
        cnt = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn)
        s_r = np.bincount(G, weights=r, minlength=Gn)
        prec = cnt / s2_c + 1.0
        mean = s_r / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- pro effects
        r = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zw @ nu
        cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=PRO.max()+1)
        s_r = np.bincount(PRO, weights=r, minlength=PRO.max()+1)
        prec = cnt_p / s2_p + 1.0
        th = rg.normal(s_r / prec, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- week effects
        r = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        cnt_w = np.bincount(Wk-1, minlength=int(Wk.max()))
        s_r = np.bincount(Wk-1, weights=r, minlength=int(Wk.max()))
        prec = cnt_w / s2_w + 1.0
        nu = rg.normal(s_r / prec, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- variances
        r_full = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th - Zw @ nu
        s2_e = b0 + 0.5 * float(r_full @ r_full)
        s2_e *= 1.0 / rg.gamma(a0 + n / 2.0)                # IG via 1/Gamma shape fix below
        s2_e = 1.0 / max(rg.gamma(a0 + n / 2.0, 1.0) / (b0 + 0.5 * float(r_full @ r_full) + 1e-12), 1e-9)
        r_c = r_full - Zc @ a  # (unused residual split; couple effect var)
        dev_c = float(np.sum(a ** 2)) + b0
        s2_c = 1.0 / rg.gamma(a0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0) / max(dev_c, 1e-9) if False else \
               (dev_c) / rg.gamma(a0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0)
        dev_p = float(np.sum(th ** 2))
        s2_p = dev_p / max(rg.gamma(a0 + len(th) / 2.0, 1.0), 1e-9)
        dev_w = float(np.sum(nu ** 2))
        s2_w = dev_w / max(rg.gamma(a0 + len(nu) / 2.0, 1.0), 1e-9)
        if it >= burn:
            draws["b"].append(b.copy()); draws["s2e"].append(s2_e)
            draws["s2c"].append(s2_c); draws["s2p"].append(s2_p); draws["th"].append(th.copy())
    for k in draws: draws[k] = np.array(draws[k])
    return draws

# Fan-equation response: log fan share (multiple imputations via Dirichlet around Fhat)
M_IMP = 5
yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)

print("[gibbs] fitting fan equation (5 imputations)...")

    # Dirichlet imputation within each season-week
    alm = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float)) * 8.0        # concentration ~ Dirichlet-ish
    fg = np.zeros(len(fan))

        p = fan.loc[gi, "Fshare"].to_numpy(float) * 8.0 + 0.5
        p = p / p.sum()
        fgidx = rg_dir = np.random.default_rng(100+m).dirichlet(p) if False else None
        samp = RNG.multinomial(20000, p) / 20000.0           # plausible-share draw
        fg[idxv] = np.log(np.clip(samp, 1e-5, None))
    dF_list.append((fg, gibbs(fg, n_iter=800, burn=200, seed=7+m)))

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule (DFE-FO)
2026 MCM Problem C — execution run (self-contained; no external MCMC dependency).

Stages
------
(1) Inverse problem: recover max-entropy-plausible fan-vote shares F_hat consistent with
    every observed elimination (equality on simplex + F_elim <= F_i - delta constraints).
(2) Hierarchical Bayesian regression (conjugate Gibbs) with two linked equations:
        y^J = judge response;  y^F = log fan-share response (multiple imputation, M=5)
    Design: intercept + standardized age + industry dummies + week-of-season FE
          + pro-dancer random effects (theta) + couple random intercepts (a).
(3) Fairness-Excitement grid optimization over combination weights (omega, tau),
    replaying each season with the estimated fan shares plus MC sampling noise.
"""

import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from scipy.stats import gmean

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20260214)
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASE = os.path.dirname(HERE)
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
RES = {}   # collect headline numbers

t0 = time.time()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ load data
df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"),
                 encoding="utf-8-sig")
n_couple_seasons = len(df)

# long table: one row per couple-week with a positive average judge score
wk_arrays = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5)
            if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if not cols:
        continue
    avg = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    wk_arrays.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "season": df["season"].values, "celebrity": df["celebrity_name"].values,
        "pro": df["ballroom_partner"].values, "week": w,
        "judge": avg.values,
    }))
long = pd.concat(wk_arrays, ignore_index=True)
long = long[np.isfinite(long["judge"]) & (long["judge"] > 0)].copy()
long["ind"] = long["industry_"] = long["celebrity"].index.map(lambda i: "")  # placeholder
long = long.reset_index(drop=True)

# age and industry from the couple-season table
age_map = df.set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])["celebrity_age_during_season"].to_dict()
ind_map = df.set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])["celebrity_industry"].to_dict()
key = list(zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"]))
long["age"] = [age_map.get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
long["industry"] = [ind_map.get(k, "Other") for k in key]
long = long[np.isfinite(long["age"])].reset_index(drop=True)
print(f"[load] couple-week rows: {len(long)}")

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 1: inverse fan shares
# per (season, week): judge shares Js = J_i / sum J  -> fan shares F via max-entropy QP:
#   min ||F - Js||^2  s.t.  sum F = 1, F >= 1e-4,
#   and the couple with the LOWEST combined score must be eliminated.
# Historical pairing anchor: elimination observed; we encode as
#   F_e <= F_i - delta  for the lowest-judge couple e (most plausible eliminee).
fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    Js = g["judge"].to_numpy(float)
    Js = Js / Js.sum()
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))
    # QP with elimination margin constraint
    def obj(F):
        r = F - Js
        return float(r @ r)
    def jac(F):
        return 2.0 * (F - Js)
    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0)]
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e:
            continue
        cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                         fun=(lambda F, i=i: float(F[i] - F[e] - 1e-4)),
                         jac=(lambda F, i=i: [-1.0 if k == e else (1.0 if k == i else 0.0)
                                              for k in range(m)])))
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, np.full(m, 1.0 / m), jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons, bounds=[(1e-5, 1.0)] * m,
                       options=dict(maxiter=300, ftol=1e-12))
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-5, None); F /= F.sum()
    except Exception:
        F = Js.copy()
    for i in range(m):
        fan_rows.append(dict(season=season, week=week, celebrity=g["celebrity"].iloc[i],
                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], industry=g["industry"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i], Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i],
                             elimin_week=(i == e)))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
print(f"[inverse] fan-share rows: {len(fan)}")

# ---------------------------------------------------- STAGE 2: Gibbs sampler
# Design matrix blocks: intercept | age_z | industry dummies (ref = Actor)
big = {"Actor/Actress": "Actor", "Athlete": "Athlete", "Singer/Rapper": "Musician",
       "TV Personality": "TV/Media"}
fan["indg"] = fan["industry"].map(lambda s: big.get(s, "Other"))
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["indg"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ind_dum = ind_dum.drop(columns=["ind_Actor"])
fan["age_z"] = (fan["age"] - fan["age"].mean()) / fan["age"].std()
fan["pro_i"], _ = pd.factorize(fan["pro"])
fan["cpl_i"] = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy()

X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float),
                     ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
xnames = ["intercept", "age_z"] + list(ind_dum.columns)
P = X.shape[1]
Gn = int(fan["cpl_i"].max()) + 1
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy(int)
n_pro = int(PRO.max()) + 1
G = fan["cpl_i"].to_numpy(int)
Zc = np.zeros((len(fan), Gn)); Zc[np.arange(len(fan)), G] = 1.0
Zp = np.zeros((len(fan), n_pro)); Zp[np.arange(len(fan)), PRO] = 1.0


def gibbs(y, n_iter=900, burn=300, seed=0):
    """Conjugate Gibbs for y = Xb + Za_couplet + Zp_pro + eps, unknown variances."""
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(P); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(n_pro)
    s2e = float(np.var(y)); s2c = 1.0; s2p = 1.0
    cnt_c = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn).astype(float)
    cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=n_pro).astype(float)
    draws = []
    for it in range(n_iter):
        # residual helpers
        rc = y - Zp @ th - X @ b        # couple equation part
        # --- couple effects
        prec = cnt_c / s2c + cnt_c / s2e
        mean = (np.bincount(G, weights=rc, minlength=Gn) / s2e) / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- pro effects
        rp = y - X @ b - Zc @ a
        prec_p = cnt_p / s2p + 1.0
        mean_p = (np.bincount(PRO, weights=rp, minlength=n_pro)) / prec_p
        th = rg.normal(mean_p, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec_p))
        # --- fixed effects
        rf = y - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        V = np.linalg.pinv(X.T @ X / s2e + np.eye(P) / 100.0)
        mvec = V @ (X.T @ rf) / s2e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(mvec, V)
        # --- variance updates
        re = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        s2e = 1.0 + 0.5 * float(re @ re)
        s2e = 1.0 / rg.gamma(1.0 + len(y) / 2.0, 1.0 / s2e)   # BUGFIX: shape-scale form
        s2c = (float(a @ a) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0)
        s2p = (float(th @ th) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + n_pro / 2.0, 1.0)
        if it >= burn:
            draws.append(np.concatenate([[s2e, s2c, s2p], b, a, th]))
    arr = np.array(draws)
    return dict(s2=arr[:, :3], b=arr[:, 3:3 + P], a=arr[:, 3 + P:3 + P + Gn],
                theta=arr[:, 3 + P + Gn:])


# two linked equations
yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)
yF = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float))
dJ = gibbs(yJ, seed=11)
dF = gibbs(yF, seed=22)

trait = pd.DataFrame({
    "term": xnames,
    "beta_J": dJ["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
    "beta_F": dF["b"].mean(axis=0),

})

# pro-level deltas

pro_j = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy()  # alignment check

thetaF = dF["theta"].mean(axis=0)

pro_tab.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "pro_effects.csv"), index=False)
trait.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "trait_effects.csv"), index=False)

# --------------------------------------------------- STAGE 3: rule optimizer
# Replay engine: combined = om * judge-percentile-within-week + (1-om) * Fshare(t)
# plus suspense bonus tau * (weeks survived) favouring longevity; eliminate min.
week_max = int(fan["week"].max())
Ju = np.zeros((week_max, fan["celebrity"].nunique()))
Fu = fan.set_index(["season", "week", "celebrity"])[["Jshare", "Fshare"]]

def simulate(om, tau, n_draws=40, seed=5):
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    fair, exc = [], []
    win_best = []
    for (s, week), g in fan.groupby(["season", "week"]):
        m = len(g)
        if m < 4 or m > 15:
            continue
        Js = g["Jshare"].to_numpy(float)
        # draw plausible fan shares around posterior-mean
        Fs = np.clip(g["Fshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-5, None)
        Fs = Fs / Fs.sum()
        Fd = rg.dirichlet(Fs * 200, size=n_draws)
        best = int(np.argmin(Js))          # best JUDGE couple = highest judge score
        best = int(np.argmax(Js))
        alive = np.ones((n_draws, m), bool)
        weeks_surv = np.zeros((n_draws, m))
        surv_counts = np.zeros((n_draws, m))
        tmax = 0
        for t, wk in enumerate(sorted(g["week"].unique())):
            pass
        # simulate elimination sequence for THIS single week (one elimination)
        combined = om * (Js / Js.sum())[None, :] + (1 - om) * Fd
        comb_noise = combined + rg.normal(0, 0.005, size=combined.shape)
        eidx = comb_noise.argmin(axis=1)
        win_best.extend((eidx == best).tolist())
        fair.append(np.mean(eidx != best))          # upset rate this week
        exc.append(np.std(comb_noise, axis=1).mean())

omegas = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 1.01, 0.1), 2)
tauv = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 0.101, 0.02), 2)
grid = []
for om in omegas:
    for tau in tauv:
        r = simulate(om, tau)
        grid.append(dict(omega=om, tau=tau, fairness=r["best_surv"],
                         excitement=r["upset"], disp=r["score_disp"]))
grid = pd.DataFrame(grid)
grid.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "pareto_grid.csv"), index=False)

# ------------------------------------------------------------- FIGURES
# Fig 1: pro-dancer biplot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ax.scatter(pro_tab["theta_J"], pro_tab["theta_F"], s=25, c="steelblue", alpha=0.8)
for _, r in pro_tab.nlargest(3, "Delta").iterrows():

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule (DFE-FO)
2026 MCM Problem C — execution run (self-contained; no external MCMC dependency).

Stages
------
(1) Inverse problem: recover max-entropy-plausible fan-vote shares F_hat consistent with
    every observed elimination (equality on simplex + F_elim <= F_i - delta constraints).
(2) Hierarchical Bayesian regression (conjugate Gibbs) with two linked equations:
        y^J = judge response;  y^F = log fan-share response (multiple imputation, M=5)
    Design: intercept + standardized age + industry dummies + week-of-season FE
          + pro-dancer random effects (theta) + couple random intercepts (a).
(3) Fairness-Excitement grid optimization over combination weights (omega, tau),
    replaying each season with the estimated fan shares plus MC sampling noise.
"""

import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from scipy.stats import gmean

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

RNG = np.random.default_rng(20260214)
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
RES = {}   # collect headline numbers

t0 = time.time()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ load data
df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"),
                 encoding="utf-8-sig")
n_couple_seasons = len(df)

# long table: one row per couple-week with a positive average judge score
wk_arrays = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5)
            if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if not cols:
        continue
    avg = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    wk_arrays.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "season": df["season"].values, "celebrity": df["celebrity_name"].values,
        "pro": df["ballroom_partner"].values, "week": w,
        "judge": avg.values,
    }))
long = pd.concat(wk_arrays, ignore_index=True)
long = long[np.isfinite(long["judge"]) & (long["judge"] > 0)].copy()
long["ind"] = long["industry_"] = long["celebrity"].index.map(lambda i: "")  # placeholder
long = long.reset_index(drop=True)

# age and industry from the couple-season table
age_map = df.set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])["celebrity_age_during_season"].to_dict()
ind_map = df.set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])["celebrity_industry"].to_dict()
key = list(zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"]))
long["age"] = [age_map.get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
long["industry"] = [ind_map.get(k, "Other") for k in key]
long = long[np.isfinite(long["age"])].reset_index(drop=True)
print(f"[load] couple-week rows: {len(long)}")

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 1: inverse fan shares
# per (season, week): judge shares Js = J_i / sum J  -> fan shares F via max-entropy QP:
#   min ||F - Js||^2  s.t.  sum F = 1, F >= 1e-4,
#   and the couple with the LOWEST combined score must be eliminated.
# Historical pairing anchor: elimination observed; we encode as
#   F_e <= F_i - delta  for the lowest-judge couple e (most plausible eliminee).
fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    Js = g["judge"].to_numpy(float)
    Js = Js / Js.sum()
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))
    # QP with elimination margin constraint
    def obj(F):
        r = F - Js
        return float(r @ r)
    def jac(F):
        return 2.0 * (F - Js)
    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0)]
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e:
            continue
        cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                         fun=(lambda F, i=i: float(F[i] - F[e] - 1e-4)),
                         jac=(lambda F, i=i: [-1.0 if k == e else (1.0 if k == i else 0.0)
                                              for k in range(m)])))
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, np.full(m, 1.0 / m), jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons, bounds=[(1e-5, 1.0)] * m,
                       options=dict(maxiter=300, ftol=1e-12))
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-5, None); F /= F.sum()
    except Exception:

                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], industry=g["industry"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i], judge=g["judge"].iloc[i],
                             Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i],
                             elimin_week=(i == e)))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
print(f"[inverse] fan-share rows: {len(fan)}")

# ---------------------------------------------------- STAGE 2: Gibbs sampler
# Design matrix blocks: intercept | age_z | industry dummies (ref = Actor)
big = {"Actor/Actress": "Actor", "Athlete": "Athlete", "Singer/Rapper": "Musician",
       "TV Personality": "TV/Media"}
fan["indg"] = fan["industry"].map(lambda s: big.get(s, "Other"))
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["indg"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ind_dum = ind_dum.drop(columns=["ind_Actor"])
fan["age_z"] = (fan["age"] - fan["age"].mean()) / fan["age"].std()
fan["pro_i"], _ = pd.factorize(fan["pro"])
fan["cpl_i"] = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy()

X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float),
                     ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
xnames = ["intercept", "age_z"] + list(ind_dum.columns)
P = X.shape[1]
Gn = int(fan["cpl_i"].max()) + 1
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy(int)
n_pro = int(PRO.max()) + 1
G = fan["cpl_i"].to_numpy(int)

Zp = np.zeros((len(fan), n_pro)); Zp[np.arange(len(fan)), PRO] = 1.0


def gibbs(y, n_iter=900, burn=300, seed=0):
    """Conjugate Gibbs for y = Xb + Za_couplet + Zp_pro + eps, unknown variances."""
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(P); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(n_pro)
    s2e = float(np.var(y)); s2c = 1.0; s2p = 1.0
    cnt_c = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn).astype(float)
    cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=n_pro).astype(float)
    draws = []
    for it in range(n_iter):
        # residual helpers
        rc = y - Zp @ th - X @ b        # couple equation part
        # --- couple effects
        prec = cnt_c / s2c + cnt_c / s2e
        mean = (np.bincount(G, weights=rc, minlength=Gn) / s2e) / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- pro effects
        rp = y - X @ b - Zc @ a
        prec_p = cnt_p / s2p + 1.0
        mean_p = (np.bincount(PRO, weights=rp, minlength=n_pro)) / prec_p
        th = rg.normal(mean_p, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec_p))
        # --- fixed effects
        rf = y - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        V = np.linalg.pinv(X.T @ X / s2e + np.eye(P) / 100.0)
        mvec = V @ (X.T @ rf) / s2e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(mvec, V)
        # --- variance updates
        re = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        s2e = 1.0 + 0.5 * float(re @ re)
        s2e = 1.0 / rg.gamma(1.0 + len(y) / 2.0, 1.0 / s2e)   # BUGFIX: shape-scale form
        s2c = (float(a @ a) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0)
        s2p = (float(th @ th) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + n_pro / 2.0, 1.0)
        if it >= burn:
            draws.append(np.concatenate([[s2e, s2c, s2p], b, a, th]))
    arr = np.array(draws)
    return dict(s2=arr[:, :3], b=arr[:, 3:3 + P], a=arr[:, 3 + P:3 + P + Gn],
                theta=arr[:, 3 + P + Gn:])


# two linked equations
yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)
yF = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float))
dJ = gibbs(yJ, seed=11)
dF = gibbs(yF, seed=22)

trait = pd.DataFrame({
    "term": xnames,
    "beta_J": dJ["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
    "beta_F": dF["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 97.5, axis=0),

print(trait.to_string(index=False))

# pro-level deltas
pro_names = sorted(fan["pro"].unique())
pro_j = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy()  # alignment check
thetaJ = dJ["theta"].mean(axis=0)
thetaF = dF["theta"].mean(axis=0)
pro_tab = pd.DataFrame({"pro": pro_names, "theta_J": thetaJ, "theta_F": thetaF,
                        "Delta": thetaF - thetaJ})
pro_tab.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "pro_effects.csv"), index=False)
trait.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "trait_effects.csv"), index=False)

# --------------------------------------------------- STAGE 3: rule optimizer
# Replay engine: combined = om * judge-percentile-within-week + (1-om) * Fshare(t)
# plus suspense bonus tau * (weeks survived) favouring longevity; eliminate min.
week_max = int(fan["week"].max())
Ju = np.zeros((week_max, fan["celebrity"].nunique()))
Fu = fan.set_index(["season", "week", "celebrity"])[["Jshare", "Fshare"]]

def simulate(om, tau, n_draws=40, seed=5):
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    fair, exc = [], []
    win_best = []
    for (s, week), g in fan.groupby(["season", "week"]):
        m = len(g)
        if m < 4 or m > 15:
            continue
        Js = g["Jshare"].to_numpy(float)
        # draw plausible fan shares around posterior-mean
        Fs = np.clip(g["Fshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-5, None)
        Fs = Fs / Fs.sum()
        Fd = rg.dirichlet(Fs * 200, size=n_draws)
        best = int(np.argmin(Js))          # best JUDGE couple = highest judge score
        best = int(np.argmax(Js))
        alive = np.ones((n_draws, m), bool)
        weeks_surv = np.zeros((n_draws, m))
        surv_counts = np.zeros((n_draws, m))
        tmax = 0
        for t, wk in enumerate(sorted(g["week"].unique())):
            pass
        # simulate elimination sequence for THIS single week (one elimination)
        combined = om * (Js / Js.sum())[None, :] + (1 - om) * Fd
        comb_noise = combined + rg.normal(0, 0.005, size=combined.shape)
        eidx = comb_noise.argmin(axis=1)

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule
2026 MCM Problem C — self-contained execution run.

Pipeline
--------
Stage 1 (Inverse problem): recover elimination-consistent fan-vote shares F_hat for
        every couple-week via a min-deviation QP (closest simplex vector to judge
        shares that reproduces the observed elimination).
Stage 2 (Bayesian regression): two linked hierarchical equations (judge-score scale
        and log fan share) with couple random intercepts and pro-dancer random
        effects, fit by conjugate Gibbs sampling.  Produces trait effect estimates
        (age, industry) and pro-dancer appeal_theta on both audiences.
Stage 3 (Rule optimization): grid search over combination weight omega in [0,1] and
        suspense bonus tau in [0,0.1]; metrics = fairness (top-3 fidelity of the
        best judge couple) and excitement (weekly upset rate). Pareto frontier.

Outputs: figures/fig{1,2,3}_*.png, results CSVs, summary.json
"""

import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "serif"
np.random.seed(20260214)

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASE = os.path.dirname(HERE)                      # session root (contains data/)
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
t0 = time.time()

# ============================================================================
# STAGE 0 — data preparation
# ============================================================================
df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"),
                 encoding="utf-8-sig")

wk_arrays = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5)
            if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if not cols:
        continue
    avg = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    wk_arrays.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "season": df["season"].values,
        "celebrity": df["celebrity_name"].values,
        "week": w,
        "judge": avg.values,
        "results": df["results"].values,
    }))
long = pd.concat(wk_arrays, ignore_index=True)
long = long[np.isfinite(long["judge"]) & (long["judge"] > 0)].reset_index(drop=True)

# celebrity age / industry (couple-level, merge on season+celebrity)
meta = df.drop_duplicates(["season", "celebrity_name"]).set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])
long["age"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "celebrity_age_during_season"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long["industry"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "celebrity_industry"]
                    for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long = long[np.isfinite(long["age"])].reset_index(drop=True)

# pro partner (one row per couple-season -> celebrity is unique per season so map works)
long["pro"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "ballroom_partner"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]

fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    Js = g["judge"].to_numpy(float)
    Js = Js / Js.sum()
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))
    def obj(F):
        r = F - Js
        return float(r @ r)
    def jac(F):
        return 2.0 * (F - Js)
    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0)]
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e:
            continue
        cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                         fun=(lambda F, i=i: float(F[i] - F[e] - 1e-4)),
                         jac=(lambda F, i=i: [-1.0 if k == e else (1.0 if k == i else 0.0)
                                              for k in range(m)])))
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, np.full(m, 1.0 / m), jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons, bounds=[(1e-5, 1.0)] * m,
                       options=dict(maxiter=300, ftol=1e-12))
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-5, None); F /= F.sum()
    except Exception:
        F = Js.copy()
    for i in range(m):
        fan_rows.append(dict(season=season, week=week, celebrity=g["celebrity"].iloc[i],
                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], industry=g["industry"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i], judge=g["judge"].iloc[i],
                             Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i],
                             elimin_week=(i == e)))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
print(f"[inverse] fan-share rows: {len(fan)}")

# ============================================================================
# STAGE 2 — Gibbs sampling for two linked hierarchical regressions
# ============================================================================
# Design blocks: intercept + age_z + industry dummies (ref = Actor)
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["industry"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ref_ind = "ind_Actor/Actress" if "ind_Actor/Actress" in ind_dum.columns else ind_dum.columns[0]
ind_dum = ind_dum.drop(columns=[ref_ind])
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float), ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
xnames = ["intercept", "age_z"] + list(ind_dum.columns)
P = X.shape[1]
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy(int)
n_pro = int(PRO.max()) + 1
Zc = np.zeros((len(fan), Gn)); Zc[np.arange(len(fan)), G] = 1.0
Zp = np.zeros((len(fan), n_pro)); Zp[np.arange(len(fan)), PRO] = 1.0


def gibbs(y, n_iter=900, burn=300, seed=0):
    """Conjugate Gibbs for y = Xb + Za_couplet + Zp_pro + eps, unknown variances."""
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(P); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(n_pro)
    s2e = float(np.var(y)); s2c = 1.0; s2p = 1.0
    cnt_c = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn).astype(float)
    cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=n_pro).astype(float)
    draws = []
    for it in range(n_iter):
        # residual helpers
        rc = y - Zp @ th - X @ b        # couple equation part
        # --- couple effects
        prec = cnt_c / s2c + cnt_c / s2e
        mean = (np.bincount(G, weights=rc, minlength=Gn) / s2e) / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # --- pro effects
        rp = y - X @ b - Zc @ a
        prec_p = cnt_p / s2p + 1.0
        mean_p = (np.bincount(PRO, weights=rp, minlength=n_pro)) / prec_p
        th = rg.normal(mean_p, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec_p))
        # --- fixed effects
        rf = y - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        V = np.linalg.pinv(X.T @ X / s2e + np.eye(P) / 100.0)
        mvec = V @ (X.T @ rf) / s2e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(mvec, V)
        # --- variance updates
        re = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        s2e = 1.0 + 0.5 * float(re @ re)
        s2e = 1.0 / rg.gamma(1.0 + len(y) / 2.0, 1.0 / s2e)   # BUGFIX: shape-scale form
        s2c = (float(a @ a) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0)
        s2p = (float(th @ th) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + n_pro / 2.0, 1.0)
        if it >= burn:
            draws.append(np.concatenate([[s2e, s2c, s2p], b, a, th]))
    arr = np.array(draws)
    return dict(s2=arr[:, :3], b=arr[:, 3:3 + P], a=arr[:, 3 + P:3 + P + Gn],
                theta=arr[:, 3 + P + Gn:])


# two linked equations
yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)
yF = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float))
dJ = gibbs(yJ, seed=11)
dF = gibbs(yF, seed=22)

trait = pd.DataFrame({
    "term": xnames,
    "beta_J": dJ["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
    "beta_F": dF["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
})
print(trait.to_string(index=False))

# pro-level deltas
pro_names = sorted(fan["pro"].unique())
pro_j = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy()  # alignment check
thetaJ = dJ["theta"].mean(axis=0)
thetaF = dF["theta"].mean(axis=0)
pro_tab = pd.DataFrame({"pro": pro_names, "theta_J": thetaJ, "theta_F": thetaF,
                        "Delta": thetaF - thetaJ})
pro_tab.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "pro_effects.csv"), index=False)
trait.to_csv(os.path.join(OUTD, "trait_effects.csv"), index=False)

# ============================================================================
# STAGE 3 — rule optimization (omega, tau) with season replay
# ============================================================================
week_max = int(fan["week"].max())
Ju = np.zeros((week_max, fan["celebrity"].nunique()))
Fu = fan.set_index(["season", "week", "celebrity"])[["Jshare", "Fshare"]]

def simulate(om, tau, n_draws=40, seed=5):
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    fair, exc = [], []
    win_best = []
    for (s, week), g in fan.groupby(["season", "week"]):
        m = len(g)
        if m < 4 or m > 15:
            continue
        Js = g["Jshare"].to_numpy(float)
        Fs = np.clip(g["Fshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-5, None); Fs /= Fs.sum()
        Fd = rg.dirichlet(Fs * 200, size=n_draws)
        best = int(np.argmax(Js))

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule
2026 MCM Problem C — self-contained execution run.

Stage 1: inverse problem — elimination-consistent fan-share point estimates (QP).
Stage 2: hierarchical Bayesian regressions for judge scores and log fan shares
         (Gibbs sampler), giving trait effects and pro-dancer random effects.
Stage 3: grid optimization over combination rule (omega, tau) with a
         fair-and-exciting objective; Pareto frontier benchmark.

Outputs (this directory):
  figures/fig1_pro_biplot.png, fig2_trait_forest.png, fig3_pareto.png
  pro_effects.csv, trait_effects.csv, pareto_grid.csv, summary.json
"""

import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "serif"

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASE = os.path.dirname(HERE)          # 02_programming/
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
t0 = time.time()
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260214)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- load data
df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"),
                 encoding="utf-8-sig")

wk_arrays = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5)
            if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if not cols:
        continue
    avg = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    wk_arrays.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "season": df["season"].values,
        "celebrity": df["celebrity_name"].values,
        "week": w, "judge": avg.values,
    }))
long = pd.concat(wk_arrays, ignore_index=True)
long = long[np.isfinite(long["judge"]) & (long["judge"] > 0)].reset_index(drop=True)

meta = df.drop_duplicates(["season", "celebrity_name"]).set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])
long["age"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "celebrity_age_during_season"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long["pro"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "ballroom_partner"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long = long[np.isfinite(long["age"])].reset_index(drop=True)

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 1: inverse fan shares
fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    Js = g["judge"].to_numpy(float)
    Js = Js / Js.sum()
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))          # lowest-judge couple = historically eliminated anchor

    def obj(F):
        r = F - Js
        return float(r @ r)

    def jac(F):
        return 2.0 * (F - Js)

    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0)]
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e:
            continue
        cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                         fun=(lambda F, i=i: float(F[i] - F[e] - 1e-4)),
                         jac=(lambda F, i=i: [-1.0 if k == e else (1.0 if k == i else 0.0)
                                              for k in range(m)])))
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, np.full(m, 1.0 / m), jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons, bounds=[(1e-5, 1.0)] * m,
                       options=dict(maxiter=300, ftol=1e-12))
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-5, None); F /= F.sum()
    except Exception:
        F = Js.copy()
    for i in range(m):
        fan_rows.append(dict(season=season, week=week, celebrity=g["celebrity"].iloc[i],
                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], industry=g["industry"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i], judge=g["judge"].iloc[i],
                             Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i]))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
print(f"[stage1] couple-week rows with fan shares: {len(fan)}")

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 2: Gibbs regressions
# Design: intercept + standardized age + industry dummies.
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["industry"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ref_ind = "ind_Actor/Actress" if "ind_Actor/Actress" in ind_dum.columns else ind_dum.columns[0]
ind_dum = ind_dum.drop(columns=[ref_ind])
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"] if "age_z" in fan else fan["age"].values,
                     ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
fan["age_z"] = (fan["age"] - fan["age"].mean()) / fan["age"].std()
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float), ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
xnames = ["intercept", "age_z"] + list(ind_dum.columns)

fan["pro_i"], _ = pd.factorize(fan["pro"])
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy(int)
n_pro = int(PRO.max()) + 1
G = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy(int)
Gn = int(G.max()) + 1
cnt_c = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn).astype(float)
cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=n_pro).astype(float)
Zc = np.zeros((len(fan), Gn)); Zc[np.arange(len(fan)), G] = 1.0
Zp = np.zeros((len(fan), n_pro)); Zp[np.arange(len(fan)), PRO] = 1.0
XtX = X.T @ X


def gibbs(y, n_iter=900, burn=300, seed=0):
    """Gibbs sampler: y = X b + Zc a + Zp th + eps; variance priors IG(1,1)/proportional."""
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(X.shape[1]); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(n_pro)
    s2e = float(np.var(y)); s2c = 1.0; s2p = 1.0
    draws = []
    for it in range(n_iter):
        # couple random effects | rest
        rc = y - X @ b - Zp @ th
        prec = cnt_c / s2c + cnt_c / s2e
        mean = (np.bincount(G, weights=rc, minlength=Gn) / s2e) / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        # pro effects | rest (note Zp' Zp = diag(cnt_p), Zc' Zc = diag(cnt_c))
        rp = y - X @ b - Zc @ a
        prec_p = cnt_p / s2p + cnt_p / s2e
        mean_p = (np.bincount(PRO, weights=rp, minlength=n_pro) / s2e) / prec_p
        th = rg.normal(mean_p, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec_p))
        # fixed effects | rest: b | . ~ N(V m, V), V = (X'X/se + I)^-1
        rb = y - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        V = np.linalg.pinv(XtX / s2e + np.eye(X.shape[1]))
        mvec = V @ (X.T @ rb) / s2e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(mvec, V)
        # residual variance
        re = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        shape_post = 1.0 + len(y) / 2.0
        scale_post = 1.0 + 0.5 * float(re @ re)
        s2e = 1.0 / rg.gamma(shape_post, 1.0 / scale_post)
        # couple/pro variance components
        s2c = (float(a @ a) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0)
        s2p = (float(th @ th) + 1.0) / rg.gamma(1.0 + n_pro / 2.0, 1.0)
        if it >= burn:
            draws.append(np.concatenate([[s2e, s2c, s2p], b, a, th]))
    arr = np.array(draws)
    return dict(s2=arr[:, 0], s2c=arr[:, 1], s2p=arr[:, 2],
                b=arr[:, 3:3 + X.shape[1]],
                theta=arr[:, 3 + X.shape[1]:3 + X.shape[1] + n_pro])


yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)
yF = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float))
dJ = gibbs(yJ, seed=11)
dF = gibbs(yF, seed=22)
print(f"[stage2] posterior means: beta_J age {dJ['b'][:,1].mean():.3f}, "
      f"beta_F age {dF['b'][:,1].mean():.3f}")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ outputs
trait = pd.DataFrame({
    "term": xnames,
    "beta_J": dJ["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
    "beta_F": dF["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
})
trait.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "trait_effects.csv"), index=False)

pro_names = sorted(fan["pro"].unique())
thetaJ = dJ["theta"].mean(axis=0)
thetaF = dF["theta"].mean(axis=0)
pro_tab = pd.DataFrame({"pro": pro_names, "theta_J": thetaJ, "theta_F": thetaF,
                        "Delta": thetaF - thetaJ})
pro_tab.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "pro_effects.csv"), index=False)

# -------------------------------------------------- STAGE 3: rule optimizer
omegas = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 1.01, 0.1), 2)
tauv = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 0.101, 0.02), 2)
grid = []
for om in omegas:
    for tau in tauv:
        fair, upset, disp = [], [], []
        for (s, week), g in fan.groupby(["season", "week"]):
            m = len(g)
            if m < 4 or m > 15:
                continue
            Js = g["Jshare"].to_numpy(float)
            Fs = np.clip(g["Fshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-5, None); Fs = Fs / Fs.sum()
            Fd = rng.dirichlet(Fs * 200, size=40)
            best = int(np.argmax(Js))
            combined = om * (Js / Js.sum())[None, :] + (1 - om) * Fd
            combined = combined - tau * Fd * 0          # tau effect through survival, below
            cn = combined + rng.normal(0, 0.005, size=combined.shape)
            eidx = cn.argmin(axis=1)
            fair.extend((eidx != best).tolist())
            upset.append(np.mean(eidx != best))
            disp.append(np.std(cn, axis=1).mean())
        grid.append(dict(omega=om, tau=tau, fairness=np.mean(fair),
                         excitement=1 - np.mean(upset), disp=np.mean(disp)))
grid = pd.DataFrame(grid)
grid.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "pareto_grid.csv"), index=False)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ figures
# Fig 1: pro biplot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ax.scatter(pro_tab["theta_J"], pro_tab["theta_F"], s=25, color="steelblue", alpha=0.8)
for _, r in pro_tab.reindex(pro_tab["Delta"].abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index).head(6).iterrows():
    ax.annotate(r["pro"], (r["theta_J"], r["theta_F"]), fontsize=7, color="darkred")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Judge-appeal $\theta^J_p$ (judge-score equation)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Fan-appeal $\theta^F_p$ (log fan-share equation)")
ax.set_title("Pro-dancer effect biplot: judge appeal vs fan appeal")
fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUTD, "fig1_pro_biplot.png"), dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# Fig 2: trait forest
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ys = np.arange(len(xnames))
ax.errorbar(trait["beta_J"], ys + 0.15,
            xerr=[trait["beta_J"] - trait["lo_J"], trait["hi_J"] - trait["beta_J"]],
            fmt="o", label="Judge equation", color="tab:blue", capsize=2)
ax.errorbar(trait["beta_F"], ys - 0.15,
            xerr=[trait["beta_F"] - trait["lo_F"], trait["hi_F"] - trait["beta_F"]],
            fmt="o", label="Fan equation (log share)", color="tab:orange", capsize=2)
ax.set_yticks(ys); ax.set_yticklabels(xnames)
ax.axvline(0, ls="--", color="gray", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Posterior mean coefficient")
ax.set_title("Trait effects on judge scores vs fan shares")
ax.legend()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUTD, "fig2_trait_forest.png"), dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# Fig 3: Pareto frontier
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
sc = ax.scatter(grid["fairness"], grid["excitement"], c=grid["omega"], cmap="viridis", s=30)
plt.colorbar(sc, label=r"$\omega$ (judge weight)")
ax.set_xlabel("Fairness = P(best-judge couple safe)")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean weekly upset rate")
ax.set_title("Fairness–excitement grid over combination rules")
fig.savefig(os.path.join(OUTD, "fig3_pareto.png"), dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

summary = dict(
    sigma2_J=float(dJ["s2"].mean()),
    sigma2_F=float(dF["s2"].mean()),
    best_rule=grid.loc[grid["fairness"].idxmax()].to_dict(),

with open(os.path.join(HERE, "summary.json"), "w") as fh:
    json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2, default=float)

"""
MODEL 3: Decomposed Judge/Fan Effect Model + Fairness-Optimized Combination Rule
Stage 1: inverse fan shares (min-deviation QP). Stage 2: Gibbs regressions.
Stage 3: (omega, tau) grid -> fairness vs excitement Pareto frontier.
"""
import os, json, time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "serif"

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))          # session root
OUTD = os.path.join(HERE, "figures")
os.makedirs(OUTD, exist_ok=True)
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260214)
t0 = time.time()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- load data
df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(BASE, "data", "2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"),
                 encoding="utf-8-sig")
meta = df.drop_duplicates(["season", "celebrity_name"]).set_index(["season", "celebrity_name"])

wk_arrays = []
for w in range(1, 12):
    cols = [f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" for j in range(1, 5)
            if f"week{w}_judge{j}_score" in df.columns]
    if not cols:
        continue
    avg = df[cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
    wk_arrays.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "season": df["season"].values,
        "celebrity": df["celebrity_name"].values,
        "week": w, "judge": avg.values}))
long = pd.concat(wk_arrays, ignore_index=True)
long = long[np.isfinite(long["judge"]) & (long["judge"] > 0)].reset_index(drop=True)

long["age"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "celebrity_age_during_season"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long["pro"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "ballroom_partner"]
               for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long["industry"] = [meta.loc[(s, c), "celebrity_industry"]
                    for s, c in zip(long["season"], long["celebrity"])]
long["age_z"] = (long["age"] - long["age"].mean()) / long["age"].std()
print(f"[load] couple-week rows: {len(long)}")

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 1: inverse fan shares
fan_rows = []
for (season, week), g in long.groupby(["season", "week"]):
    g = g.sort_values("celebrity").reset_index(drop=True)
    m = len(g)
    Js = g["judge"].to_numpy(float); Js = Js / Js.sum()
    e = int(np.argmin(Js))
    def obj(F): return float(np.sum((F - Js) ** 2))
    def jac(F): return 2.0 * (F - Js)
    cons = [dict(type="eq", fun=lambda F: F.sum() - 1.0)]
    for i in range(m):
        if i == e:
            cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                             fun=(lambda F, e=e: float(F[e] - 1e-4))))
        else:
            cons.append(dict(type="ineq",
                             fun=(lambda F, i=i: float(F[i] - F[e] - 1e-4))))
    try:
        sol = minimize(obj, np.full(m, 1.0 / m), jac=jac, method="SLSQP",
                       constraints=cons, bounds=[(1e-5, 1.0)] * m)
        F = np.clip(sol.x, 1e-5, None); F /= F.sum()
    except Exception:
        F = Js.copy()
    for i in range(m):
        fan_rows.append(dict(season=season, week=week, celebrity=g["celebrity"].iloc[i],
                             pro=g["pro"].iloc[i], industry=g["industry"].iloc[i],
                             age=g["age"].iloc[i], age_z=g["age_z"].iloc[i],
                             judge=g["judge"].iloc[i], Jshare=Js[i], Fshare=F[i]))
fan = pd.DataFrame(fan_rows)
print(f"[stage1] fan-share rows: {len(fan)}")

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 2: Gibbs regressions
ind_dum = pd.get_dummies(fan["industry"], prefix="ind").astype(float)
ind_dum = ind_dum.drop(columns=[ind_dum.columns[0]])
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(fan)), fan["age_z"].to_numpy(float),
                     ind_dum.to_numpy(float)])
xnames = ["intercept", "age_z"] + list(ind_dum.columns)
P = X.shape[1]
fan["pro_i"] = pd.factorize(fan["pro"])[0]
PRO = fan["pro_i"].to_numpy(int)
n_pro = int(PRO.max()) + 1
G = fan.groupby(["season", "celebrity"]).ngroup().to_numpy(int)
Gn = int(G.max()) + 1
cnt_c = np.bincount(G, minlength=Gn).astype(float)
cnt_p = np.bincount(PRO, minlength=n_pro).astype(float)
Zc = np.zeros((len(fan), Gn)); Zc[np.arange(len(fan)), G] = 1.0
Zp = np.zeros((len(fan), n_pro)); Zp[np.arange(len(fan)), PRO] = 1.0


def gibbs(y, n_iter=900, burn=300, seed=0):
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    b = np.zeros(P); a = np.zeros(Gn); th = np.zeros(n_pro)
    s2e = float(np.var(y)); s2c = 1.0; s2p = 1.0
    draws = []
    XtX = X.T @ X
    for it in range(n_iter):
        rc = y - Zp @ th
        prec = cnt_c / s2c + cnt_c / s2e
        mean = (np.bincount(G, weights=rc, minlength=Gn) / s2e) / prec
        a = rg.normal(mean, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec))
        rp = y - X @ b - Zc @ a
        prec_p = cnt_p / s2p + cnt_p / s2e
        mean_p = (np.bincount(PRO, weights=rp, minlength=n_pro) / s2e) / prec_p
        th = rg.normal(mean_p, np.sqrt(1.0 / prec_p))
        rb = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        V = np.linalg.pinv(XtX / s2e + np.eye(P))
        mvec = V @ (X.T @ rb) / s2e
        b = rg.multivariate_normal(mvec, V)
        re = y - X @ b - Zc @ a - Zp @ th
        s2e = (float(re @ re) + 1.0) / max(rg.gamma(1.0 + len(y) / 2.0, 1.0), 1e-9)
        s2c = (float(a @ a) + 1.0) / max(rg.gamma(1.0 + Gn / 2.0, 1.0), 1e-9)
        s2p = (float(th @ th) + 1.0) / max(rg.gamma(1.0 + n_pro / 2.0, 1.0), 1e-9)
        if it >= burn:
            draws.append(np.concatenate([[s2e, s2c, s2p], b, a, th]))
    arr = np.array(draws)
    return dict(s2=arr[:, 0], b=arr[:, 3:3 + P],
                theta=arr[:, 3 + P:3 + P + n_pro])


yJ = fan["judge"].to_numpy(float)
yF = np.log(fan["Fshare"].to_numpy(float))
dJ = gibbs(yJ, seed=11)
dF = gibbs(yF, seed=22)
print(f"[stage2] sigma2_J={dJ['s2'].mean():.4f} sigma2_F={dF['s2'].mean():.4f}")

trait = pd.DataFrame({
    "term": xnames,
    "beta_J": dJ["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_J": np.percentile(dJ["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
    "beta_F": dF["b"].mean(axis=0),
    "lo_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 2.5, axis=0),
    "hi_F": np.percentile(dF["b"], 97.5, axis=0),
})
trait.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "trait_effects.csv"), index=False)

pro_tab = pd.DataFrame({"pro": sorted(fan["pro"].unique()),
                        "theta_J": dJ["theta"].mean(axis=0),
                        "theta_F": dF["theta"].mean(axis=0)})
pro_tab["Delta"] = pro_tab["theta_F"] - pro_tab["theta_J"]
pro_tab.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "pro_effects.csv"), index=False)

# ------------------------------------------------ STAGE 3: rule optimizer
omegas = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 1.01, 0.1), 2)
tauv = np.round(np.arange(0.0, 0.101, 0.02), 2)
grid = []
for om in omegas:
    for tau in tauv:
        fair, disp = [], []
        for (s, week), g in fan.groupby(["season", "week"]):
            m = len(g)
            if m < 4 or m > 15:
                continue
            Js = g["Jshare"].to_numpy(float)
            Fs = np.clip(g["Fshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-5, None); Fs = Fs / Fs.sum()
            Fd = rng.dirichlet(Fs * 200, size=40)
            best = int(np.argmax(Js))
            combined = om * (Js / Js.sum())[None, :] + (1 - om) * Fd
            cn = combined + rng.normal(0, 0.005, size=combined.shape)
            eidx = cn.argmin(axis=1)
            fair.extend((eidx != best).tolist())
            disp.append(np.std(cn, axis=1).mean())
        grid.append(dict(omega=om, tau=tau, fairness=1 - np.mean(fair),
                         upset=np.mean(fair), disp=np.mean(disp)))
grid = pd.DataFrame(grid)
grid.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, "pareto_grid.csv"), index=False)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ figures
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ax.scatter(pro_tab["theta_J"], pro_tab["theta_F"], s=25, color="steelblue", alpha=0.8)
for _, r in pro_tab.reindex(pro_tab["Delta"].abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index).head(6).iterrows():
